items.title: Report IS03688, Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration Program Update (carried text YF-EV-0118)

citations.finding: R asks the Infrastructure Committee to recommend to City Council that the Attachment 5 approach be approved. The report is labelled 'Council decision required'.
citations.establishes: The text of R and the route by which it could reach Council: only if the committee carried it.
citations.quote: That the updated approach for the remaining routes under the Active Transportation Network Expansion Program, as outlined in Attachment 5 ... be approved.

citations.finding: Recommendation 1 asks for approval of the approach in Attachment 5. Administration's 'Next Step' recommends that the approach 'be adjusted as outlined in Attachment 5'.
citations.establishes: That administration recommended the Attachment 5 approach to the committee, for recommendation on to Council.

citations.finding: In 2026 administration still described the programme's approved budget as $100 million and said its recommendations required no change to CM-20-0330. Nothing indicates a base high enough to put the 2024 motion's remainder in the band.
citations.establishes: Corroborates a base of about $100M.
citations.quote: $100 million was approved to rapidly expand the City's active transportation network.

citations.finding: Recommendation 1 asks Infrastructure Committee to recommend approval of the updated approach in Attachment 5; the report says Council decision is required.
citations.establishes: The text and intended recipient of Recommendation 1.
citations.quote: That Infrastructure Committee recommend to City Council: That the updated approach for the remaining routes ... be approved.

citations.finding: The August 2026 report describes the approved program capital budget as $100 million.
citations.establishes: The reported original approved program amount used for the stated illustrative arithmetic.
citations.quote: $100 million was approved to rapidly expand the City’s active transportation network.

citations.finding: Recommendation 1 asks Infrastructure Committee to recommend City Council approval of the updated approach in Attachment 5. The report labels the action 'Council decision required' and says the recommendation would require no change to capital profile CM-20-0330 or its borrowing bylaws.
citations.establishes: What administration recommended, to whom, and its stated budget effect.

items.title: REPLACEMENT Attachment 3, IS03688, Locations and Status Updates (carried text YF-EV-0226); original at DocumentId 304029

citations.finding: According to Attachment 3, as of 2026-08-10 none of the 14 listed entries had started construction. They were recorded as tendered but not started, as no longer viable for 2026, or as having no delivery plan.
citations.establishes: That all 14 listed routes were unbuilt at the primary status date.
citations.quote: Tender awarded. Construction has not yet started.

citations.finding: Attachment 3 states its statuses are accurate as of August 10, 2026. Listed locations are described as not yet started, not viable for 2026 installation, paused for reconsideration, or having no delivery plan; none is reported as under construction or complete.
citations.establishes: The listed routes were unbuilt at the report’s specified status date, including the 50 Street segment paused for reconsideration.
citations.quote: These routes may be revisited using alternate design approaches or other future initiatives.

citations.finding: Attachment 3 dates its statuses August 10. It records the 84 Avenue and 92A Avenue entries as tendered but not started; the 93 Street/84 Avenue entry under a different combined description as tendered but not started; six other entries as formerly scheduled for 2026 but no longer viable for 2026 installation; and the remaining five as having no delivery plan or schedule. None is recorded as under construction or complete.
citations.establishes: The listed routes’ reported construction status as of August 10, 2026.

items.title: REPLACEMENT (Version 2) Attachment 5, IS03688, Modified Approach (carried text YF-EV-0140)

citations.finding: The declared primary version of Attachment 5 (Version 2) provides for evaluating the remaining routes and reporting back in Q1 2027 'for Council direction and approval'. It does not state in terms that construction of the listed routes waits for that step, so under the primary definition what R proposed was not a hold.
citations.establishes: The treatment R proposed under Version 2.
citations.quote: The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications.

citations.finding: Version 2, the declared primary, describes evaluation and a Q1 2027 report 'for Council direction and approval'. It does not say that construction or advancement of the listed routes waits for that report, and it contains no removal language.
citations.establishes: That under the primary version the recommendation is re-evaluation plus a report back, not an express freeze.
citations.quote: If Council approves the approach, the following projects may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.

citations.finding: Three of the 14 entries join several street segments under one bullet. Splitting them would give 18 routes, not 14.
citations.establishes: That '14' depends on counting by bullet, which is the brief's fixed rule.

citations.finding: Version 2 says the remaining routes will be evaluated and that Administration will bring a Q1 2027 report for Council direction and approval; it does not expressly state that construction or advancement waits for that step.
citations.establishes: The recommendation’s treatment does not meet the brief’s primary express-deferral test.
citations.quote: The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications. In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report ... for Council direction and approval.

citations.finding: Recommendation 1 requests approval of Attachment 5’s updated approach. Version 2 lists 14 entries under projects that may be re-evaluated; the entries are 50 Street (101 Avenue–109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue–Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 Avenue–101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 Street–83 Street); 85 Street (93 Avenue–98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 Street–96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue–Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road–85 Street); 93 Street (82 Avenue–84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street–89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 Street–75 Street) and 75 Street (94 Avenue–94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 Street–163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street–west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street–west of 84 Street); and Grovenor (148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street segments).
citations.establishes: Recommendation 1 requests approval of the approach, and Version 2 lists 14 entries for possible re-evaluation.
citations.quote: If Council approves the approach, the following projects may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.

citations.finding: Version 2 does not state that listed routes must wait for its evaluation or Q1 2027 report before construction or advancement; it says they may be re-evaluated if Council approves the approach.
citations.establishes: The express-deferral element of the normalized proposition is not established by the operative text.
citations.quote: The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications.

citations.finding: Version 2 says the remaining routes will be evaluated and that administration will bring options to Council in Q1 2027. It does not expressly state that construction or advancement of the 14 listed routes must wait for that report or a Council decision.
citations.establishes: The treatment proposed in the declared primary version of R.

citations.finding: Version 2 lists these 13 routes as continuing: 50 Street (109A Avenue to Goldbar Park Road); 84 Avenue (Mill Creek Ravine to 91 Street); 100 Street (76 Avenue to 80 Avenue); 107 Avenue (east of Groat Road to 163 Street); 110 Avenue/90 Street and 112 Avenue; 111 Avenue (120 to 121 Street); 114 Avenue (81 to 89 Street); 127 Avenue (97 to 102A Street); 163 Street (87 to 95 Avenue); 163 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue); 167/169 Street (Whitemud Drive to 87 Avenue); Kingsway (113 to 122 Street); and Victoria Park Road (116 Street to River Valley Road). It separately lists 14 entries for possible reevaluation.
citations.establishes: The two route lists and their counts in the declared primary version.

citations.finding: Version 2’s operative wording is: 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications. In Q1 2027, Administration will bring forward a report outlining trade-offs and options for the remaining routes, including an update on the remaining funding and budget implications, for Council direction and approval.' Its route list says the projects 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' Neither passage expressly says construction or advancement waits.
citations.establishes: The missing express deferral in the declared primary version.

items.title: Attachment 5, IS03688, Modified Approach (original; carried text YF-EV-0222)

citations.finding: The original Attachment 5 would remove the 14 listed projects from the programme's scope for 2026 and 2027, to be revisited only after evaluation and subject to funding. That is an express deferral, and under the stricter reading a removal.
citations.establishes: That the original version meets both deferral readings for exactly 14 listed entries.
citations.quote: the following projects would be removed from the scope of the Active Transportation Network Expansion Program for 2026 and 2027.

citations.finding: The original and Version 1 use stronger scope-removal language for the listed routes, while Version 2 replaces that treatment with possible re-evaluation and a later report. Thus the answer depends on the operative version.
citations.establishes: Version 2’s treatment differs materially from the original and Version 1.
citations.quote: If Council approves the recommended change in approach, the following projects would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027.

citations.finding: The 14 entries listed apart, identical across all three versions, are 50 Street (101 to 109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 to 101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 to 83 Street); 85 Street (93 to 98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 to 96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street); 93 Street (82 to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 to 89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 to 94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 to 163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); and Grovenor: 148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street. The original expressly removes these from programme scope for 2026 and 2027.
citations.establishes: The route names, count and treatment in the original version.

items.title: City Council Budget Minutes, 2023-11-21 and continuations, items 5.1.1 and 5.1.2, Capital Budget Amendment 2 (carried text YF-EV-0211)
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk

citations.finding: Principe (mover) and Rice (seconder) moved to reduce CM-20-0330 by $50,000,000 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt'. Council defeated it 4 to 8. On a $100,000,000 base it would have left $50,000,000 (reviewer's calculation).
citations.establishes: One jointly brought, defeated motion that leaves about $50M and names a debt reduction as its destination.
citations.quote: be reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt.

citations.finding: At the November 21, 2023 budget meeting, Councillor Principe moved and Councillor Rice seconded a $50 million reduction to CM-20-0330; Council defeated it 4–8. The motion stated that the funding reduction would come from tax-supported debt.
citations.establishes: One jointly brought motion to reduce the program was put and defeated; its text identifies the reduction in tax-supported debt.
citations.quote: That capital profile CM-20-0330 ... be reduced by $50,000,000 ... with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt. ... Defeated (4 to 8)

citations.finding: At the November 21–29, 2023 budget meeting, Capital Budget Amendment 2 as put was moved by Principe and seconded by Rice: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt.' Hamilton, Cartmell, Rice and Principe voted in favour; Knack, Paquette, Sohi, Salvador, Tang, Rutherford, Stevenson and Wright opposed. It was defeated 4–8.
citations.establishes: The first operative motion, roles, destination, vote and defeat.

citations.finding: The November 2023 original amendment said the $50,000,000 would go 'towards the tax levy', but Council voted on a restated amendment specifying a reduction from tax-supported debt. The withdrawn Rice/Principe amendment for $26,808,000 was neither a recorded defeat nor explicitly a CM-20-0330 cut.
citations.establishes: The destination in the text actually voted on and why the withdrawn amendment is not a third qualifying attempt.

items.title: City Council Minutes, 2026-09-08 (continuation 2026-09-16), item 11.6 (carried text YF-EV-0227)

citations.quote: Laid Over: September 8, 2026, City Council to October 6, 2026, City Council

citations.quote: Laid Over: September 8, 2026, City Council to October 6, 2026, City Council

citations.finding: At City Council’s September 8 meeting, item 11.6 was a notice seeking future budget options for the routes listed for reevaluation; it was laid over to October 6. It was not approval of R.
citations.establishes: The recorded status of the related notice at Council, not a decision on the administration recommendation.

items.title: Infrastructure Committee Minutes, 2026-08-26, item 7.6 (meeting page; carried text YF-EV-0209)
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk

citations.finding: The minutes of item 7.6 record no motion to adopt R, whether moved, put or carried. The committee did not adopt administration's recommendation.
citations.establishes: Non-adoption of R by the Infrastructure Committee on 2026-08-26.

citations.finding: The only substantive motion incompatible with R was defeated on a 2 to 2 tie. Its text: continue at the previously approved scope of CM-20-0330, advance tender-ready routes, and schedule 2027 construction at the earliest opportunity. No motion to adopt R was put and defeated, so the committee did not 'reject' R as the brief defines it.
citations.establishes: The committee neither adopted R nor carried a motion to proceed against it.
citations.quote: In Favour (2) | A. Salvador, and M. Janz; Opposed (2) | E. Rutherford, and R. Clarke; Defeated (2 to 2)

citations.finding: The minutes list the Version 2 replacement among the item 7.6 attachments. The committee defeated Councillor Salvador’s motion to continue the program under its previously approved scope, 2–2, but the minutes record no motion adopting or incompatibly rejecting Recommendation 1.
citations.establishes: The committee’s recorded disposition and which Attachment 5 version was before it.
citations.quote: Motion, put: ... Continue implementation ... in accordance with the previously approved scope ... Defeated (2 to 2)

citations.finding: Infrastructure Committee item 7.6 records no motion adopting Recommendation 1. Rutherford’s amendment to remove accelerated construction language lost 2–2: Rutherford and Clarke in favour; Salvador and Janz opposed. Salvador’s motion to continue the previously approved CM-20-0330 scope, advance tender-ready routes and prepare 2027 procurement then lost 2–2: Salvador and Janz in favour; Rutherford and Clarke opposed. Knack and Paquette, though committee members present during portions of the meeting, cast neither of those votes. Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright attended as non-members and could not vote on item 7.6.
citations.establishes: The motions, recorded votes and results at the committee meeting.

citations.finding: The only substantive motion put at item 7.6 sought to continue the previously approved scope and was defeated. Its defeat did not adopt a hold or carry a decision incompatible with R.
citations.establishes: The committee left R without a substantive decision under the brief’s definitions.

items.title: City Council Budget Minutes, 2024-12-02 and continuations, items 5.1.1 and 5.1.2, Capital Budget Amendment 2 (carried text YF-EV-0212)
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk

citations.finding: Principe (mover) and Rice (seconder) moved to decrease CM-20-0330 by $33,650,000 in each of 2025 and 2026. Council defeated it 4 to 7.
citations.establishes: A second jointly brought reduction motion, on a separate occasion, that was defeated.
citations.quote: be decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery

citations.finding: On a $100,000,000 base, the 2024 motion would have left $32,700,000, not about $50M (reviewer's calculation). It was a larger cut than the holder described.
citations.establishes: That the second motion fails the primary $45M–$55M band.

citations.finding: At the December 2, 2024 budget meeting, Principe moved and Rice seconded a reduction of $33.65 million in each of 2025 and 2026, totaling $67.3 million; Council defeated it 4–7. Against a $100 million baseline, the reviewer’s arithmetic gives $32.7 million remaining, not about $50 million.
citations.establishes: The second jointly brought motion was defeated but does not meet the primary $45–55 million remainder band on the $100 million baseline.
citations.quote: be decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 ... Defeated (4 to 7)

citations.finding: At the December 2–5, 2024 budget meeting, Capital Budget Amendment 2 was moved by Principe and seconded by Rice: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery of the Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 project.' Cartmell, Rice, Rutherford and Principe voted in favour; Knack, Sohi, Salvador, Janz, Tang, Stevenson and Wright opposed. It was defeated 4–7.
citations.establishes: The second operative motion, roles, destination, vote and defeat.

citations.finding: The December 2024 motion named two $33,650,000 decreases, totaling $67,300,000. Against the $100,000,000 approved capital budget, the reviewer-calculated remainder is $32,700,000, below the primary $45 million–$55 million band.
citations.establishes: Why the second motion fails the primary amount requirement.

citations.finding: Version 1 keeps rules 1a and 1b, which remove routes affecting travel lanes or parking from the programme. The same 14 entries are listed apart.
citations.establishes: That Version 1 meets the primary deferral reading.
citations.quote: Routes that impact travel lanes will be removed from the Active Transportation Network Expansion Program

citations.finding: Version 1 says the listed projects 'may be revisited using alternate design approaches or other future initiatives.' Its general approach removes routes that affect travel lanes or parking, but does not say every one of the 14 named entries has that effect. The original differs: it says the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027.'
citations.establishes: Version sensitivity and the limit of Version 1’s route-specific wording.

citations.quote: for $100,000,000 ... to fund planning, design, and delivery ... with funding coming from Tax-Supported Debt.

items.title: Bike routes cancelled or put off despite council direction

citations.finding: Taproot reports that councillors 'simply received the report for information'. That describes the item as having no substantive decision. The carried minutes contain no motion to receive the report.
citations.establishes: That the outcome was reported as receipt for information, which is consistent with 'left without a decision'.

items.title: Edmonton city council rejects proposed changes to remaining bike routes

citations.finding: Global News reported that councillors 'elected to stay the course' and that the 'Committee kept the current plan as is'. This is a media characterisation that matches the holders' account; it is not a record of any motion.
citations.establishes: That the outcome was reported as the committee keeping the existing plan. It does not establish any motion or vote.

items.title: City capital financial update, September 30, 2024, Attachment 2

citations.finding: Council approved capital profile CM-20-0330 for $100,000,000 during its November 30–December 2022 budget meeting. A City capital financial update for September 30, 2024 still reports a $100,000,000 current approved budget. The later profile records a $430,000 reduction in 2025, after both candidate motions.
citations.establishes: The contemporaneous $100,000,000 capital-budget base for the December 2024 calculation.
